To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed a new synthetic route for very small iron oxide nanoparticles, (2) we have demonstrated that the magnetic properties of these particles are very high, (3) we have shown that they can be easily transferred from the organic to an aqueous medium and, (4) that these particles have the potential to be used as specific reporters for molecular imaging.
we report the synthesis of very-small gamma Fe2O 3 nanoparticles (5nm) presenting very narrow size distribution and exceptionally-high saturation magnetization.
the synthesis of very stable and monodisperse gamma Fe2O 3 nanoparticles in a water-soluble form is possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new ultrasmall iron-oxide-based particles as potential T1 contrast agents for molecular imaging.
the synthesis and characterization of very small magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles with very high magnetic properties and their potential use as specific contrast agents for molecular MRI.
the synthesis, characterisation, and application of ultrasmall iron oxides as T1 MRI contrast agent for Molecular Imaging.

the particles are very promising candidates for MRI applications, in particular for molecular imaging, and their synthesis can be readily scaled up.
the synthesis of ultrasmall iron oxides in organic solvents followed by transfer to water is a viable route for the preparation of very promising T1 MRI contrast materials.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthesis of these particles can be performed in a simple, fast and scalable way and that the particles are suitable as potential contrast agents for molecular imaging.

the synthesis method developed in this work allows the preparation of ultrasmall iron nanoparticles in a single step and in a very reproducible manner, with high magnetisation and narrow size distribution.

the use of a simple organic solvent and the addition of an organic ligand during the nanoparticle synthesis is a simple way to obtain very small and stable iron oxide nanoparticles with exceptional properties for molecular imaging.

the synthesis of ultrasmall iron nanoparticles with high magnetization is possible, and that these nanoparticles are suitable as contrast agents for MRI.
